title: MPQ: A Message-Passing View of Post-Training Quantization
claim: Prior solvers commit hard decisions one unit at a time; ours keeps soft beliefs across all units, then commits at the end.
layout: 2 stacked panels (a) prior, (b) ours; left-to-right flow with a feedback loop
description: The figure has a header strip showing a weight row w split into blocks w1..wB, plus a legend of three colored codeword squares (blue, pink, tan). Panel (a), 'Greedy (GPTQ / LDLQ)', shows three grids of checkbox candidates for Blocks 1-3. Arrows labeled 'Error feedback' lead from grid to grid, and each step checks one more block, so blocks are committed sequentially. Panel (b), 'MPQ', is a left-to-right pipeline. A 'Discrete denoiser' box holds per-block bar charts of codeword probabilities. These feed a 'Gaussian linear module' box that shows the calibration Hessian H = X^T X and couples all blocks. The output goes to an 'Updated beliefs' box with changed bars, then to 'Marginal MAP' hard codewords, then to 'Exact block CD'. A 'Repeat soft updates' arrow loops back. The eye lands first on the stacked gray panels and the colored bars and checkmarks.
caption: {Greedy quantization and MPQ. Rows represent weight blocks $b$. Colors identify codewords $c\in\mathcal C_b$, and bar heights show probabilities $q_b^t(c)$ (Eq. [ref]). (a) Greedy solvers fix blocks sequentially and pass error to remaining blocks. (b) MPQ alternates denoising and Gaussian linear updates across all blocks, then applies marginal MAP projection and exact block CD.}
abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a key technique for efficiently deploying large language models, as it compresses weights into low-bit representations without retraining. Existing PTQ solvers, including GPTQ, LDLQ, and block coordinate descent, commit each weight block to a single codeword before its neighbors are considered, leaving near-optimal alternatives unexplored. In this work, we cast row-wise PTQ as posterior inference over discrete codebooks, in which existing solvers correspond to a zero-temperature, hard-decision limit retaining only the top codeword per block. We propose Message-Passing Quantization (MPQ), which preserves soft posterior information across blocks during inference and commits to hard codewords only at the output stage. MPQ first uses vector approximate message passing to compute approximate blockwise posteriors, then refines a hard-decision initialization by exact block coordinate descent. Across 2-bit lattice and 3- and 4-bit scalar quantization on dense language models from Llama, Qwen, and Mistral families, MPQ improves perplexity and zero-shot accuracy over strong hard-decision baselines, and composes favorably with preprocessing techniques such as activation-aware scaling and incoherence processing. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/poseidonchan/MPQ.
